sources.facts: The original 1880 survey plate, printed between pp. 574 and 575, records hilltop, lower west line, three reservoirs and mosque position.
The government survey describes three masonry lines and round towers on the projecting portions. Upper curtains averaged fourteen feet. The surrounding scarp is mostly natural rock.
Entry 16 describes main levels Malaygarh, Kamargarh and Asirgarh, a stepped western approach, a massed southwest bastion, pointed parapet battlements and a pointed doorway.
District heritage record confirms the three-level fort and the dark stone Jami mosque.
Written conservation report documents the Faruqi mosque and its triple-arched south-east courtyard gateway, rubble buttress and vaults.
Archaeological Survey’s national list binds Asirgarh in Burhanpur to its fort walls, Sat Darwaza, mosque and temple.
